newsitem.title: USA: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies steady to lower.

text.p: Early calls on CME lean hog futures ranged from 0.200 cent per lb lower to 0.100 higher while pork belly futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Some analysts look for pressure in hog futures following steady to lower cash hog indications and lower wholesale pork prices late last week. Packers should keep bids down in view of the drop in cutout values, they said.
USDA reported pork cut-out values fell $0.59 to $0.66 per cwt on Friday.
However, others look for a further upward correction as they see tighter hog supplies through the summer and likely stronger cash markets as packers compete for available supplies.

Pork belly futures could see some carryover support from futures gains posted on Friday but most analysts look for pressure linked to weaker cash belly price quotes on Friday. Continued tight storage supplies were seen as supportive but demand for cash bellies will have to improve to provide further buying incentives, sources said.
USDA quoted fresh pork bellies in the $83 to $85 per cwt level for 14-16 lbs.
